content.user_title: Build Azure Event Grid Java Apps
content.value_statement: Azure Event Grid integration can be hard to wire correctly in Java applications. This skill gives focused SDK patterns for publishing, receiving, parsing, and handling events.
actual_capabilities: Shows the Maven dependency for azure-messaging-eventgrid 4.27.0.
Demonstrates EventGridPublisherClient setup with API keys.
Provides Java examples for EventGridEvent and CloudEvent publishing.
Shows parsing examples for EventGridEvent and CloudEvent payloads.
Covers namespace receive, acknowledge, reject, and release flows.
limitations: Does not deploy Azure resources or create Event Grid topics.
Uses placeholder endpoints, keys, and event payloads.
Does not include full application projects or tests.
Does not validate tenant permissions, quotas, or pricing.

use_cases.title: Add Event Publishing
use_cases.description: Use concise Java SDK examples to publish EventGridEvent and CloudEvent messages from an application.

use_cases.title: Compare Event Schemas
use_cases.description: Review native Event Grid, CloudEvents, and custom payload options before choosing an integration pattern.

use_cases.title: Handle Namespace Delivery
use_cases.description: Use receive, acknowledge, reject, and release patterns for Event Grid namespace subscriptions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Publisher Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Java service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to set up an Azure Event Grid publisher client in Java using the Azure SDK.

prompt_templates.title: Publish CloudEvents
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate event publishing with a standard schema.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me publish CloudEvents from a Java service to Azure Event Grid, including the important event fields.

prompt_templates.title: Parse Incoming Events
prompt_templates.scenario: Webhook or receiver handling for event consumers.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to parse incoming EventGridEvent and CloudEvent payloads in Java and map event data to typed classes.

prompt_templates.title: Design Pull Delivery Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java workflow for receiving events from an Event Grid namespace topic and deciding when to acknowledge, reject, or release them.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to publish an order-created event from a Java service.
output_examples.output: A concise implementation plan that covers the publisher client, event schema choice, event fields, and send operation.

output_examples.input: An architect asks whether to use EventGridEvent or CloudEvent for a new integration.
output_examples.output: A comparison of native Event Grid events, CloudEvents, and custom payloads with practical selection guidance.

output_examples.input: A platform engineer asks how to process namespace events safely.
output_examples.output: A receive-loop outline that explains lock tokens, successful acknowledgements, rejects, releases, and delayed retries.

best_practices: Use DefaultAzureCredential or managed identity when possible instead of long-lived access keys.
Batch related events when it improves throughput and stays within Event Grid size limits.
Use stable event IDs and clear schemas to support idempotent consumers.
anti_patterns: Hard-coding access keys in application source files.
Publishing large payloads that exceed Event Grid size limits.
Acknowledging namespace events before processing succeeds.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy Azure Event Grid resources?
faq.answer: No. It provides Java SDK usage patterns and examples, not infrastructure deployment steps.

faq.question: Does it support CloudEvents?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for creating, publishing, and parsing CloudEvents with the Azure SDK.

faq.question: Can I use managed identity with these examples?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a DefaultAzureCredential example for Azure identity based authentication.

faq.question: Does it include async publishing?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows async publisher client usage and basic success or error handling patterns.

faq.question: Does it explain Event Grid namespaces?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers namespace receiving plus acknowledge, reject, and release operations.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: No. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the marketplace metadata.
